## Rule

ARC-GEN source `external/ARC-GEN/tasks/task_1b60fb0c.py`: a connected 4x4 creature containing `(0,0)` is drawn as three blue rotated copies on a 10x10 grid, with `offset` in `{0,1}`. The output fills the fourth rotated copy in red, except cells already overwritten by a blue copy remain blue.

The low-cost formulation reads 21 possible red target cells, reads the corresponding source cells for both offsets, infers the offset from two 4-bit stencils, and scatters `-ch0/+ch2` deltas only where the red fill is needed.

## Algorithm sketch

For target cells `T`, source banks `A` (`offset=0`) and `B` (`offset=1`):

```python
choose_b = any(row5_rev[i] > col5[i] for i in range(4))
rot = B if choose_b else A
fill = input[rot] ^ input[T]  # generator invariant: input[T] => input[rot]
output = input.copy()
output[ch0, T] += -fill
output[ch2, T] += fill
```

Exhaustive proof used for the staged candidate: all connected 4x4 shapes containing `(0,0)`, sizes 6..12, across both offsets. `any(row5_rev > col5)` matched `offset` in all 9464 cases; `input[T] and not input[rot]` had 0 hits over 198744 target cells.

## Cost analysis

Team-best source of truth is external manifest row `task027,Boladi,9e3acfe64d1fba5eedb8108bc76d14d866527a56155becee92e6924233b6da87,988,18.1043,2026-06-12T15:38:55Z` (`<TEAM_REPO>/Team_Submission/Backend/manifest.csv`), not the stale home live artifact.

Staged cost 988 = memory 604 + params 384. Dominant charged tensors are `updates [2,21] F32 = 168 B`, three stencil reads `m_f/a_f/b_f [1,21] F32 = 84 B each`, and the INT64 index initializers: `b_scatter_idx 168`, `b_here/b_a/b_b 63 each`, plus two 12-element offset-probe index banks.

The 64-byte saving vs team-best comes from deleting the weighted score plumbing (`b_weights`, `b_axes`, two Mul outputs, two ReduceSum scalars) and one 21-cell boolean mask by using the generator-proven XOR fill relation. Real-input profile matches static: `static=988 profile=988 (memory 604 + params 384; 265 real inputs)`.

Staged cost 926 = memory 570 + params 356. The saving vs 988 comes from proving 11 target cells are never already blue over the ARC-GEN random branch plus fixed official examples, so `b_here` shrinks from `[1,21,3]` to `[1,10,3]`; the `[1,10]` current mask is padded false back to `[1,21]`. Dominant charged tensors are still `updates [2,21] F32 = 168 B`, source reads `a_f/b_f [1,21] F32 = 84 B each`, `m_f_h [1,10] F32 = 40 B`, `b_scatter_idx 168`, and `b_a/b_b 63 each`. Real-input profile matches static: `static=926 profile=926 (memory 570 + params 356; 265 real inputs)`.

No absolute floor claimed. Within this formulation, further meaningful gains require avoiding the two source GatherND banks, the ScatterND index bank, or the F32 update bank without materializing a full-canvas tensor.

## Don't-do log

_Record ruled-out hypotheses here so future agents don't retry them._

- 2026-06-11 [worker-2]: single-cell/two-cell offset classifiers rejected; exhaustive connected-shape enumeration found no perfect classifier.
- 2026-06-11 [worker-2]: `sum(row5_rev) > sum(col5)` selector is correct but scores 992, dominated by `any(row5_rev > col5)` at 988.
- 2026-06-11 [worker-2]: float-difference `selected_source - current` fill is generator-safe but adds F32 intermediates and does not beat bool/XOR.
- 2026-06-11 [worker-2]: ScatterElements/flatten rewrites rejected because they require full-canvas or flat intermediates that dominate sparse ScatterND.
- 2026-06-21 [worker-7]: **Broadcast-offset synthesis (#155) of the INT64 index banks is a NET LOSS — INT64-intermediate memory tax.** Decoded the 988 banks: all four are a single 21-cell target stencil `T=[row,col]` plus tiny constant prefixes. `b_here=[1,r,c]`; `b_scatter_idx[0]=[0,0,r,c]`, `[1]=[0,2,r,c]` (rc identical to `b_here`); `b_a = 9-T` (exact rot180 about 10×10 center); `b_b = 10-T` for all cells except cell index 7 (the (5,0)→(0,0) offset wrap). So T could in principle be stored once (42 params) and the banks synthesized via Add/Concat. BUT a runtime-assembled `[N,D]` INT64 index bank is charged to **memory at 8 bytes/element** (§145: "runtime-build the index → assembled INT64 index tensor is charged as memory"), whereas an initializer costs **1 param/element**. Measured: `b_scatter_idx` 168 params (init) vs 1344 memory bytes (synthesized intermediate); `b_here` 63 vs 504. Synthesis always loses 8×. Do not pursue Option A.
- 2026-06-21 [worker-7]: **Channel-pre-slice to cut GatherND index rank 3→2 is a NET LOSS.** All 5 GatherND reads (b_here/b_a/b_b/row5/col5) read channel 1; pre-Gathering ch1 into one shared plane would let indices drop the channel column, saving ~71 params total. But the shared plane is a charged intermediate; the smallest crop covering used rows 0–7 × cols 0–9 is `[1,8,10]` = 80 B even as U8/BOOL, exceeding the 71-param save. Net ≥+9. Floor confirmed.
- 2026-06-21 [worker-7]: **Option B (symmetry-as-source / footprint PLANE) loses to the sparse banks.** The fourth copy = rot180 of a blue copy, so a Slice-negstep/Transpose could synthesize the footprint as a plane — but any `[1,*,10,10]` plane is 100–4000 B memory, far above the 357 index-bank params. Same family as the already-rejected ScatterElements/flatten dead-end. **Verdict: 988 is the structural floor for this task** — the sparse §113 GatherND/ScatterND net cannot be beaten without materializing a tensor more expensive than its own index banks.
